title: Knowledge
completion: of this book has written itself

partDescriptions.method: Ways of reading I found again. Each one takes me a little faster.
partDescriptions.memory: Things from before. I no longer know if they are true.
partDescriptions.anomaly: Sentences that should not have been there. I keep them all.
partDescriptions.intuition: Things I sense before I understand them. Each one changes the way I read.
partDescriptions.permanent: These ones I keep. Whatever happens.

sentences.smallStep: That's one small step / for man, / one giant leap / for mankind.
sentences.dogEar: A dog-eared page. / Not by me.

sentences.smallPrint: A fingerprint / smudge / on the page. / Too small / to be mine.
sentences.underlined: Someone / underlined / this line. / There is nothing / on it.
sentences.footprints: Footprints / in the dust. / They go / to the shaft. / No further.
sentences.upsideDown: A book / shelved upside down. / On purpose, / I think.

sentences.belowPages: I hear / pages turning / on the floor below. / No one / answers.
sentences.oneShoe: A shoe, / alone, / on the last step.
sentences.worn: Every page / of this book / has been read. / You can feel it / in the paper.
sentences.wallMarks: A mark / on the wall. / Then another. / I stopped / at a hundred.
sentences.myHand: My handwriting / in the margin. / I do not remember / writing it.
sentences.blankButLast: A book / of 410 blank pages. / Except / the last.
sentences.aheadDay: A book / that tells / my day. / It is / one day ahead.
sentences.closeIt: A book / where every line / says: / “Close it.”
sentences.rightToLeft: A book / written / right to left. / It reads / better / in the mirror.
sentences.noError: A book / without a single error. / The only one.
sentences.catalogue: The catalogue / of the Library. / It is wrong.
sentences.heavyShut: A book / that weighs / more / closed / than open.
sentences.doorBook: A book / where someone / looks / for a door. / The door is never found.

intuition.done: I will understand no more of it.
intuition.unknownGesture: I do not know this gesture yet.
intuition.nothingLeft: There are none left to find.

semanticFilter.name: Semantic filter
semanticFilter.description: My eye learns where meaning hides. Each level makes finds more frequent.
semanticFilter.effect: chance that a page hides a find
notes: They flee the edges. Read the middle.
Stop reading letters: read the gaps.
Meaning finds me. I no longer have to search.

ariadne.name: Ariadne's thread
ariadne.description: Finds lean more often toward the sentence I am looking for.
ariadne.effect: finds in the sentence I seek
notes: I pull a thread. At the end, always the same sentence.

sentenceMemory.name: Memory of sentences
sentenceMemory.description: I recognise what I have already read. Fewer repeats.
notes: That one, I already have. I move on.

speedReading.name: Speed reading
speedReading.description: My fingers turn the pages faster than my eyes.
speedReading.effect: leaves turning on their own per second, at most
notes: I no longer read. I leaf through, and it is enough.

muscleMemory.name: Muscle memory
muscleMemory.description: When I turn a page by hand, everything else follows.
muscleMemory.effect: per click, on top: one second of reading
notes: My gesture pulls the others along.

returnMap.name: Map of the Return
returnMap.description: When I am away, I lose less of my reading.
notes: I leave marks to find my page again.

deepSleep.name: Deep sleep
deepSleep.description: I sleep longer. The pages turn all that time.
notes: I sleep. The pages do not.

flair.name: Flair
flair.description: I can sense the books that are not like the others.
notes: That one. I don't know why, but that one.

bargain.name: Economy of gesture
bargain.description: Each method costs me a little less to learn. Without end.
notes: I no longer need to reread everything to learn.

armful.name: The Armful
armful.description: I take methods by the armful: ten, a hundred, or all I can carry.
notes: Why just one, when my arms can hold ten?

reminiscence.name: Reminiscence
reminiscence.description: What I once understood comes back on its own, as far as I had gone.
reminiscence.effect: after the Exile, intuitions come back
notes: I had understood it before. It comes back.

gestures.description: I know this gesture by heart. Each level doubles what it makes me read.

notes.diagonal: One word in two. Then one in three.
notes.finger: My finger knows where to go before I do.
notes.voice: I no longer whisper. I no longer need to.
notes.lectern: The stone holds the book. My hands are free.
notes.ladder: I no longer climb down. I read up there.
notes.cornee: I no longer look for my page. It waits for me.
notes.metronome: I no longer hear the beat. I read inside it.
notes.wheel: I barely push. It turns on its own.
notes.lift: The basket never comes down empty.
notes.automaton: It reads faster than I do. I do not hold it against it.
notes.clock: The hours are shorter. The pages, more numerous.

reminiscence.on: I let what I knew come back.
reminiscence.off: I no longer let anything come back.

diagonal.description: The eye no longer follows the line: it crosses it. One word in two is enough to guess the other, and the page empties twice as fast.
diagonal.quote: There is in every page a path shorter than the page. The old librarians called it the slope: you slide down it without reading, and reach the bottom feeling you have understood everything. They also said that those who only take the slope end up forgetting how to climb back.
diagonal.source: note in the margin of an untitled volume

finger.description: The finger holds the line like a handrail. The eye no longer goes back: it only follows.
finger.quote: They say a reader wore down his forefinger from running it under the lines. He claimed the finger reads before the eye, and the eye merely agrees. On a shelf, a book was found in which every line bore a thin brown trace, from the first page to the last.
finger.source: tale from the gallery of stairs

voice.description: The inner voice read at the speed of speech. Silenced, it lets the words pass unspoken.
voice.quote: For years I heard my own voice reading every line to me, patient, a little weary. One day it fell silent in the middle of a sentence, and the sentence went on without it. I have read faster since. But at night I sometimes listen for that voice in the silence of the hexagon, as one listens for a step on the stairs.
voice.source: torn page, found folded inside a lamp

lectern.description: A block fallen from the railing holds the book open. The arms, freed, no longer tremble.
lectern.quote: The railings have been crumbling slowly, forever. No one has ever seen a stone fall into the well, and yet stones are missing everywhere. I think they do not fall: the Library offers them, one by one, to whoever needs to set a book down.

ladder.description: The ladder rolls along the shelves. The top shelves are no longer a journey: you read without coming down.
ladder.quote: Each wall has five shelves and each shelf thirty-two books; the highest are the least read, and therefore, some say, the truest. To climb is to choose what no one has chosen. A legend tells of a reader who never came down from his ladder, and who can still be heard, some nights, turning pages above the lamps.

cornee.description: A folded corner keeps the page. Reading resumes where it stopped, without reading anything twice.
cornee.quote: I do not remember folding this page. Yet the crease is old, worn as if it had been opened a thousand times. Every time I pick up the book, it opens there, and I read as if I had never stopped.

metronome.description: A brass pendulum keeps the beat. The eye no longer looks for its rhythm: it follows it, line after line, without tiring.
metronome.quote: I found it in a niche between two shelves, covered in dust. Nobody knew what it was for. I wound it once, and it never stopped again: it still beats while I sleep, and when I wake, my eyes have already picked up its pace.

wheel.description: A wooden wheel holds twenty open books. One push, and the next one settles before my eyes.
wheel.quote: An engineer once drew this wheel for a king who wanted to read without getting up. I have no king and no kingdom, but in the end I built one out of shelf boards. The books turn before me like the sails of a windmill, and none of them ever falls.
wheel.source: after an engraving from 1588, glued into an untitled book

lift.description: A rope, a pulley, a basket in the well. Books from the other floors come up to the hexagon.
lift.quote: The well has no bottom, they say, but it has floors. I lowered a basket on a rope, and it came back up full. I do not know who fills it. I do not dare go down to look. Sometimes I thank them, softly, leaning over the railing.

automaton.description: A reader of wood and brass, seated before a book. It understands nothing, but it turns the pages, and each one counts.
automaton.quote: Its eyes are two glass marbles. Its fingers, springs. It reads without ever stopping, without ever understanding, and I sometimes wonder how it differs from the other readers of the Library. Perhaps only in this: it does not complain.

clock.description: A clock without hands links every room of the gallery. At each stroke, every open book turns a page.
clock.quote: I followed the ticking from one room to the next, for a long time, until I understood there was only one clock, hidden everywhere at once. It does not tell the time. It gives the signal. And at each signal, the whole gallery turns a page with me.
clock.source: inscription carved beneath an empty dial
